disease_label_per_paper: Presumptive neuroleptic malignant syndrome after amantadine reduction with malignant catatonia overlap and ECT response
presentation_summary: 52-year-old woman with schizoaffective disorder, cutaneous lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, CKD stage III, and seizure history presented febrile with altered mental status, lead-pipe rigidity, mutism, grasp reflex, stereotypies, tachycardia, and hypertension.
The report notes creatine kinase and WBC were within normal limits.
Within 48 hours she developed acute hypoxic respiratory failure and seizure-like activity requiring intubation; aspiration was complicated by MRSA pneumonia.
Medication history included amantadine 100 mg daily, and emergency information suggested rapid amantadine reduction.
Amantadine was restarted with partial response; after limited response to high-dose lorazepam and amantadine, urgent ECT produced rapid improvement.

risk_context.source_text_value: Emergency-room history suggested rapid reduction in amantadine.
NMS versus malignant catatonia were both considered high in the differential diagnosis.
Mutism, stereotypies, grasp reflex, catatonic symptoms, and BFCRS 24 were described.

observations.source_text_value: Rapid amantadine reduction was reported as a possible trigger.
The patient was described as febrile; exact temperature was not reported.
observations.conversion_note: Qualitative fever encoded as a conservative low fever proxy.

observations.source_text_value: Autonomic dysfunction with hypertension was present.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Presumptive diagnosis was NMS in the setting of amantadine reduction.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The authors report a presumptive NMS diagnosis based on disrupted central dopaminergic activity.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Malignant catatonia remained an important differential diagnosis.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: NMS versus malignant catatonia were both high on the differential.

confirmatory_findings.finding: MRSA pneumonia developed after aspiration but rigidity and autonomic abnormalities persisted after pneumonia improved.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Pneumonia treatment did not resolve the motor and autonomic syndrome.

confirmatory_findings.finding: EEG did not support nonconvulsive seizure as the primary explanation.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Recorded shaking events lacked electrographic correlate.

confirmatory_findings.finding: MRI, lupus cerebritis testing, meningitis workup, and urinalysis did not identify another primary cause.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The report describes unrevealing MRI and negative alternative workups.

confirmatory_findings.finding: ECT response was rapid after lorazepam and amantadine were insufficient.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: She became alert within 12 hours of the first ECT and improved further after the second.

quality_warnings: This case intentionally preserves NMS/malignant-catatonia diagnostic overlap instead of forcing the overlap into ordinary ranking evidence.
The paper's presumptive diagnosis, exclusion workup, pneumonia course, and ECT response are confirmatory/contextual and marked use_in_ranking false.
